extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evidentiary requirements for invoking the AIA prior-art exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) (common ownership and joint research agreement) during patent examination, including required statements, amendments, timing, fees, and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement to invoke joint research agreement (JRA) exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant or patent owner must provide a statement that the disclosure relied on by the rejection and the claimed invention were made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement under 35 U.S.C. 102(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must also assert that the agreement was in effect on or before the effective filing date of the claimed invention, and that the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the joint research agreement. The statement should either be on or begin on a separate sheet and must not be directed to other matters (37 CFR 1.4(c)). The statement must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). See 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)(ii)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure or amendment to disclose names of parties to JRA
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for the claimed invention must disclose or be amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) permits the specification to be amended to disclose the name of each party to the JRA as required by 35 U.S.C. 102(c)(3). If names are not already stated in the application, an amendment is necessary to include them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and processing-fee requirement for 1.71(g) amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) disclosing JRA parties must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i) unless filed within certain time windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee is waived only if the amendment is filed: (1) within three months of the filing date of a national application; (2) within three months of entry of the national stage (37 CFR 1.491) in an international application; (3) before mailing of a first Office action on the merits; or (4) before mailing of a first Office action after filing a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114. See 37 CFR 1.71(g)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing amendment after issue fee paid; certificate of correction required
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment disclosing JRA parties under 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) is filed after the issue fee is paid, the issued patent may not include the names; the patent must be corrected to include the names by certificate of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction must be by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323 for the amendment to be effective. The same correction requirement applies when the amendment is not filed until after grant. It is unnecessary to file a reissue or reexamination to submit such an amendment. See 37 CFR 1.71(g)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement format and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements invoking either common ownership or the JRA exception should be on or begin on a separate sheet and must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.4(c) requires that the statement 'should either be on or begin on a separate sheet and must not be directed to other matters.' Signatures must comply with 37 CFR 1.33(b). Clear, conspicuous placement (e.g., separate piece of paper or separately labeled section) is recommended so the examiner notices the statement quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception applies only to 102(a)(2) prior art (not 102(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) exception can only be invoked with respect to disclosures that are applied as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) (U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, or WIPO published international applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception applies when the rejection is under 102(a)(2) (anticipation) or 103 (obviousness) based on a 102(a)(2) reference. It does not apply to disclosures that qualify as prior art under 102(a)(1) (public disclosures before the effective filing date). Thus a reference that is prior art under 102(a)(1) remains available even if commonly owned or subject to a JRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception does not remove double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) exception is not effective to remove a disclosure applied as a basis for statutory or non‑statutory double patenting rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures excepted as prior art under 102(b)(2)(C) could still be the basis for statutory double patenting or obviousness-type double patenting rejections. See MPEP § 717.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception does not eliminate use of disclosure as evidence of enablement or inherency
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a disclosure is excepted under 102(b)(2)(C), it may still be used as evidence of enablement or inherency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior art exception is not effective to remove a disclosure as evidence of enablement or inherency. See MPEP § 2131.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership must exist by the effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Common ownership (or an obligation to assign to the same person(s)/organization(s)) must be shown to exist not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement of present common ownership filed after the effective filing date is not sufficient unless that statement was filed on the effective filing date. See In re Onda, 229 USPQ 235 (Comm’r Pat. 1985).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient wording to establish common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear statement identifying the application and the referenced subject matter and asserting ownership by the same person(s)/organization(s) at the time the invention was effectively filed is sufficient to establish common ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sufficient wording: 'Application [serial number] and the subject matter disclosed in the reference(s) [patent identifier] were, at the time the invention was effectively filed, owned by [name of person(s)/organization(s)].' The statement must be signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and conspicuous presentation of ownership/JRA statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements concerning common ownership or JRA invocation should be clear and conspicuous so the examiner can quickly notice them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the statement on a separate piece of paper or in a separately labeled section. Applicants may, but are not required to, submit additional supporting evidence even when the statement alone is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evidence may be required if examiner has doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner has independent evidence raising a material doubt about the accuracy of the applicant’s representation of common ownership or the existence of an obligation to assign, the examiner may require objective evidence of common ownership or assignment obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible objective evidence includes: (A) reference to assignments recorded in the USPTO (37 CFR Part 3) conveying the entire rights to the same person(s)/organization(s); (B) copies of unrecorded assignments filed in each of the applications; (C) affidavits/declarations by the common owner explaining facts supporting common ownership (signed by an empowered official); and (D) other evidence establishing common ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on applicant when examiner establishes prima facie case
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner establishes a prima facie case of unpatentability under 102(a)(2) or 103, the burden to overcome the rejection by invoking the JRA provisions of 102(b)(2)(C) and 102(c) is on the applicant or patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit the required statements and any necessary amendments or supporting evidence to invoke the exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: JRA effective-date and scope requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The joint research agreement must have been in effect on or before the effective filing date of the claimed invention, and the claimed invention must have been made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JRA is not required to be in effect on or before the prior art date of the reference whose subject matter is to be excepted. If the JRA began after the effective filing date, or if the claimed invention was not made within the scope of the JRA, the JRA exception cannot be invoked (illustrated by Examples 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4) dual pathways for treating subject matter as commonly owned
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4), subject matter that would otherwise be prior art under 102(a)(2) will be treated as commonly owned for purposes of 102(b)(2)(C) if either (i) applicant provides a statement that the subject matter and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person as of the effective filing date, or (ii) the applicant provides the JRA statement and the application discloses the names of JRA parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)(i) for the common-ownership statement pathway and 1.104(c)(4)(ii)(A)-(B) for the JRA pathway. Both routes require the statements to be timely and signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment consequences and interplay with prosecution (terminal disclaimer and double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to invoke the exception may necessitate reopening prosecution and could lead to new double patenting rejections; examiners may refuse entry of an amendment if not accompanied by a terminal disclaimer when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) is submitted in an application under final rejection to overcome a rejection based on a U.S. patent that is prior art only under 102(a)(2), the examiner may refuse to enter the amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) if it is not accompanied by an appropriate terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(d)). Withdrawal of the rejection may necessitate issuing a new double patenting rejection based on the excepted subject matter; that Office action can be made final provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced. Submissions remain subject to rules of practice (37 CFR 1.116, 1.121, 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples to illustrate proper and improper invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples show when the JRA/common-ownership exceptions will or will not apply (e.g., timing of JRA, scope of JRA activities, ownership allocations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: (1) If JRA existed prior to the effective filing date and claimed invention was made within JRA scope, the exception can be invoked (Example 1). (2) If JRA goes into effect after the application’s effective filing date, the exception cannot be invoked (Example 2). (3) If JRA exists but is limited to different activities and the claimed invention was not made as a result of activities within JRA scope, the exception cannot be invoked (Example 3). Use these factual distinctions when evaluating eligibility.
